question: Shared: prediction of conversion from MCI to AD dementia in ADNI MCI participants, with a 3-year horizon available in both papers. P-190 uses 355 ADNI-1/2/GO MCI (168 converting within 3 years, 187 non-converters followed at least 3 years) with FDG-PET deep-learning radiomics plus clinical scores. P-192 uses 415 ADNI-GO/2 aMCI with two feature sets: a biomarker set (CSF, regional amyloid PET, regional FDG-PET) and a clinical set (demographics, APOE, ADAS-Cog11, RAVLT, TMT-B, FAQ, MoCA). The PET and clinical channels are shared. Case selection (a near-balanced sample against an unselected cohort), architecture and training design (P-192 trains on CN vs dementia and applies the model to aMCI) are differences the rule allows.
metric: As recorded, a mismatch: accuracy (P-190, 90.62%) against PPV (P-192, 68.0% at 4 years). The round-20 reading says P-192 reports no AUC. That is wrong: P-192's Tables 3-4 (PDF pages 24-26, omitted from the round-20 text extract) print AUCs for both feature sets at every horizon, and accuracy for the clinical set. AUC with AUC, at the matched 3-year horizon, is the fair comparison. Accuracy depends on class balance (P-190's sample is 47% converters, P-192's cohort 21.3% at 3 years).

figures.P-190: Independent test group of 34 (16 MCI-c / 18 MCI-nc); means over repeated runs. DLR+C (FDG-PET deep features + CDRSB, MMSE, age, education, APOE): accuracy 90.62 +/- 1.16%, AUC 0.90 +/- 0.01. Hanley-McNeil for 0.90 with 16/18: Q1 = 0.818, Q2 = 0.853, SE = 0.057, CI [0.788, 1.000]. Clinical method alone: accuracy 81.09%, AUC 0.81, CI [0.660, 0.960]. FDG-PET alone: SUVR method AUC 0.68; ZF-Net deep features alone AUC 0.756, CI [0.590, 0.923]. SUVR + clinical AUC 0.85.
figures.P-192: 3-year horizon, evaluation set 291 aMCI, 21.3% converted, so 62/229. Biomarker set: RUSBoost AUC 0.77 (sensitivity 64.5%, specificity 90.3%), Hanley-McNeil SE = 0.037, CI [0.697, 0.843]; LR AUC 0.70, CI [0.621, 0.779]. Clinical set: RUSBoost AUC 0.81, accuracy 85.5%, AUC CI [0.742, 0.879]; LR AUC 0.76, accuracy 81.7%. The record's figure is the 4-year biomarker-set RUSBoost PPV 68.0% (AUC 0.77).

matched_figure_check: The headline gap is beyond uncertainty in both directions: P-190's DLR+C AUC 0.90 against P-192's 3-year biomarker AUC 0.77 (0.90 is outside [0.697, 0.843], and 0.77 is outside [0.788, 1.000]). But both papers report single-channel conditions, and there they agree. Clinical channel: P-190's clinical method (AUC 0.81) against P-192's clinical set at 3 years (RUSBoost 0.81, LR 0.76). Each lies inside the other's interval, and the accuracies (81.09% against 81.7%/85.5%) agree too. PET channel: P-190's FDG-PET-only models (deep features 0.756, SUVR 0.68) against P-192's PET/CSF biomarker set at 3 years (RUSBoost 0.77, LR 0.70), all inside each other's intervals. The whole gap therefore belongs to P-190's fusion of deep FDG-PET features with clinical scores, which P-192 never fitted. P-190's own ablation shows that step: clinical 0.81, then SUVR + clinical 0.85, then DLR + clinical 0.90.
performance_validity: Passes: P-190's 0.90/90.62% and P-192's 0.69-0.82 are below 0.97. P-190's headline rests on a single 34-subject test group, and its clinical inputs include CDRSB and MMSE, which also enter the clinical diagnosis of conversion. P-192 left MMSE, logical memory and CDR out of its clinical set to reduce this circularity.

candidate_explanations.difference: Input combination, shown by P-190 to produce the gap: adding FDG-PET deep features to its clinical model raises AUC from 0.81 to 0.90. P-192 has no combined PET + clinical model. Because a paper shows this, the pair fails condition 3.
candidate_explanations.quote: The average AUCs (±SD) of SUVR method, Clinical method, SUVR+Clinical method, and DLR+C method were 0.68 ± 0.01, 0.81 ± 0.02, 0.85 ± 0.01, and 0.90 ± 0.01, respectively, in the independent test group.

candidate_explanations.difference: Clinical feature definition: P-190's clinical inputs include CDRSB and MMSE; P-192 excludes MMSE and CDR to reduce circularity with the diagnosis.
candidate_explanations.quote: To decrease circularity with clinical diagnostic criteria, MMSE, logical memory, and CDR scores were not included in this feature set.

reason: The record sets an accuracy against a PPV, and the round-20 reading missed P-192's printed AUCs. On AUC at the matched 3-year horizon, P-190's fused model (0.90) exceeds P-192's biomarker model (0.77) beyond uncertainty. But on the single-channel conditions both papers report, they agree: clinical 0.81 against 0.81/0.76, and PET 0.756/0.68 against 0.77/0.70. P-190's own ablation attributes the gap to fusing deep PET features with clinical scores. The pair fails condition 3.

quotes.quote: Our test group consisted of 16 MCI-c subjects and 18 MCI-nc subjects, and it was used to evaluate the diagnostic value of the predictive models.
Among five methods, the DLR+C method showed the best performance with accuracy of 90.62 ± 1.16%, sensibility of 87.50 ± 0.00%, and specificity of 93.39 ± 2.19% in the independent test group.
the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, AUC, and execution time of the ZF-Net were 74.12 ± 2.32, 70.63 ± 3.02, 77.22 ± 4.10%, 0.756, and 231.20 s, respectively.

Biomarker feature set (imaging and CSF biomarkers) included variables from all modalities that contribute to creation of ATN biomarker profile: (1) all CSF biomarkers (Aβ1–42,tau, p-tau181p), (2) regional amyloid PET measures (florbetapir SUVR of 75 brain regions), (3) regional FDG PET (FDG measures from five different brain regions).

The cumulative proportions of individuals who progressed from aMCI to AD was 5.7% at 6 months, 9.9% at 1 year, 18.0% at 2 years, 21.3% at 3 years, and 22.2% at 4 years of follow-up.
